issues.legal_issue: An admitted written amendment to a partnership agreement specifying partners’ shares governs over a claim that those terms were mistaken when the party alleging mistake fails to prove it.
material_facts: An earlier partnership deed made one partner’s larger share conditional on a capital contribution and provided for a smaller share if the condition was not met.
A later deed, executed after negotiations and admitting additional partners, expressly specified equal 25% profit and loss shares for each of the two partners who brought the suit.
The defendants admitted executing the later deed but contended that the shares stated in it were a mistake and that the partners had orally agreed to smaller shares.
The later deed did not repeat the earlier deed’s capital-contribution condition, and the defendants did not establish that its stated shares failed to reflect the parties’ mutual intention.
The lower courts relied on the absence of proof that the required capital contribution had been made to limit the two partners’ combined share to 10%.
issues.conclusion: The lower courts erred in disregarding the later deed. The two partners together were entitled to 50% of the partnership’s profits and losses until their expulsion.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 17, 91 and 92 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, an admission may be relevant evidence; the terms of a written contract are proved by the document, and oral evidence generally cannot contradict, vary, add to or subtract from those terms. The first proviso to Section 92 permits proof of a mistake, but the party asserting that the written terms are mistaken bears the burden of establishing it. Roop Kumar v. Mohan Thedani, (2003) 6 SCC 595, explains the operation of Sections 91 and 92 and the primacy of an integrated written agreement; it discusses Gangabai v. Chhabubai, (1982) 1 SCC 4, and Ishwar Dass Jain v. Sohan Lal, (2000) 1 SCC 434, concerning when oral evidence may be admitted to show that a document was not intended to operate as an agreement.

predicates.appeal_from_partnership_accounting_decre: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree resolving the accounting and shares of partners.
predicates.admitted_written_amendment_sets_partner_: The parties admit executing a later written amendment that expressly states the partners’ shares.
predicates.later_deed_omits_earlier_share_condition: The later written amendment does not include a condition on shares that appeared in an earlier agreement.
predicates.party_alleging_documentary_mistake_fails: A party claims the shares stated in the written amendment were included by mistake but does not establish that claim.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns partnership accounting, the parties admit a written amendment stating their shares, the amendment omits an earlier share condition, and the party alleging a mistake fails to prove it, the partners receive the shares stated in that amendment.

issues.legal_issue: A partnership agreement’s expulsion term remains operative when a later amendment does not supersede or conflict with it, and an expulsion made under that term may be upheld.
material_facts: An earlier partnership deed authorized expulsion of a partner for specified conduct affecting the firm or its business, after a reasonable opportunity to be heard.
The later partnership deed contained no conflicting provision on expulsion.
The trial court upheld the expulsion of the partners who brought the suit, and the Supreme Court found no reason to interfere with that decision.
issues.conclusion: The expulsion of the partners was upheld, and the lower courts’ decision on that issue was maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The applicable partnership terms continued to operate to the extent that they were not superseded by the later deed. The earlier deed authorized expulsion on specified grounds after a reasonable opportunity to be heard; the Court found that the later deed did not conflict with that term and that the trial court had given sound reasons for upholding the expulsion. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this issue.

predicates.appeal_challenging_partner_expulsion: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the expulsion of a partner.
predicates.partnership_deed_authorizes_expulsion_fo: The partnership agreement authorizes expulsion for specified conduct after the affected partner has an opportunity to be heard.
predicates.later_deed_does_not_conflict_with_expuls: A later partnership agreement does not supersede or conflict with the earlier expulsion term.
predicates.trial_court_upheld_expulsion_on_its_reas: The trial court upheld the expulsion and gave reasons for doing so.

issues.definition: In an appeal challenging expulsion, the expulsion is upheld when the partnership agreement authorizes it after an opportunity to be heard, a later agreement does not conflict with that term, and the trial court upheld the expulsion on its reasons.
